title: CI/CD Deployment for the React Frontend
content:
Step 1 – Prepare the Frontend Source Code on GitHub The TechVina repository uses the master branch for automatic deployment. Verify the following project structure:
TechVina/ ├── frontend/ │ ├── package.json │ ├── package-lock.json │ ├── src/ │ └── public/ └── .github/ └── workflows/ └── deploy-frontend.yml Open the project root directory in VS Code and check the current Git branch:
git branch --show-current Expected deployment branch:
master GitHub Actions uses frontend/package-lock.json to install pinned dependencies through npm ci before building the application. The Frontend does not need to be built on EC2; the GitHub-hosted runner handles the build.
Step 2 – Configure GitHub Repository Variables Open the TechVina repository on GitHub. Select Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables. Click New repository variable and create these six variables: Repository Variable Configured value VITE_API_BASE_URL https://<CLOUDFRONT_DOMAIN> (without a trailing /) VITE_AWS_REGION ap-southeast-1 VITE_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID <COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID> VITE_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID <COGNITO_APP_CLIENT_ID> VITE_COGNITO_REDIRECT_URI https://<CLOUDFRONT_DOMAIN>/ VITE_COGNITO_LOGOUT_URI https://<CLOUDFRONT_DOMAIN>/ The CloudFront address must match the callback configuration of the Cognito App Client. Values prefixed with VITE_* become part of browser-side JavaScript; do not store AWS Access Keys, database passwords, or other secrets in these variables.
Step 3 – Configure the Frontend Deployment Workflow Open .github/workflows/deploy-frontend.yml. The workflow uses Node.js 22, GitHub OIDC (configured in section 5.8.1), and the S3/CloudFront resources in ap-southeast-1.
Configure the workflow as shown below. Replace <AWS_ACCOUNT_ID> and <CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID> with the actual AWS resource identifiers:
name: Deploy TechVina Frontend on: push: branches: - master paths: - "frontend/**" - ".github/workflows/deploy-frontend.yml" workflow_dispatch: permissions: contents: read id-token: write concurrency: group: deploy-techvina-frontend cancel-in-progress: false jobs: deploy: name: Build and deploy Frontend runs-on: ubuntu-latest defaults: run: working-directory: frontend steps: - name: Checkout source code uses: actions/checkout@v7 - name: Setup Node.js uses: actions/setup-node@v7 with: node-version: "22" cache: npm cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json - name: Install dependencies run: npm ci - name: Build Frontend env: VITE_API_BASE_URL: ${{ vars.VITE_API_BASE_URL }} VITE_AWS_REGION: ${{ vars.VITE_AWS_REGION }} VITE_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID }} VITE_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID }} VITE_COGNITO_REDIRECT_URI: ${{ vars.VITE_COGNITO_REDIRECT_URI }} VITE_COGNITO_LOGOUT_URI: ${{ vars.VITE_COGNITO_LOGOUT_URI }} run: npm run build - name: Configure AWS credentials uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6.3.0 with: role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:role/techvina-github-actions-frontend-role aws-region: ap-southeast-1 - name: Deploy to Amazon S3 run: | aws s3 sync dist/ s3://techvina-frontend-<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>/ \ --exclude "images/*" \ --no-progress \ --only-show-errors - name: Invalidate CloudFront cache run: | aws cloudfront create-invalidation \ --distribution-id <CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID> \ --paths "/*" The workflow performs the following operations in sequence:
Checkout source code: Fetch the repository source. Setup Node.js / Install dependencies: Install Node.js 22 and dependencies from package-lock.json. Build Frontend: Pass the six Repository Variables and run npm run build to generate frontend/dist/. Configure AWS credentials: Assume the techvina-github-actions-frontend-role using OIDC temporary credentials, without permanent AWS Access Keys. Deploy to Amazon S3: Synchronize the new build to techvina-frontend-<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>. Invalidate CloudFront cache: Refresh the distribution using a /* CloudFront invalidation. The --exclude "images/*" option preserves the images/ objects used in 5.6.2. The workflow also intentionally omits --delete to avoid deleting objects that are not part of the Frontend build.
The workflow triggers automatically when files under frontend/** or the Frontend workflow change on master. It can also be started manually from GitHub Actions using Run workflow.
Step 4 – Commit, Push, and Verify GitHub Actions Save the workflow, then run these commands from the repository root in VS Code’s Git Bash terminal:
git add .github/workflows/deploy-frontend.yml git commit -m "ci: update frontend deployment workflow for AWS" git push origin master Open GitHub → Actions → Deploy TechVina Frontend, select the workflow run for the pushed commit, and inspect the Build and deploy Frontend job.
During the actual TechVina deployment, after correcting the GitHub OIDC subject in the IAM Trust Policy as described in 5.8.1, the workflow was rerun successfully:
Workflow: Deploy TechVina Frontend Job: Build and deploy Frontend Commit: 250dfd0 Status: Success Total duration: 34s Verify that Install dependencies, Build Frontend, Configure AWS credentials, Deploy to Amazon S3, and Invalidate CloudFront cache all complete. If AWS authentication fails, verify the IAM Trust Policy and actual OIDC sub as documented in 5.8.1.
Step 5 – Verify the Deployed Website Open Amazon S3 → techvina-frontend-<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID> → Objects and verify index.html, assets/, and images/. Open CloudFront → Distributions and check that an invalidation was created. Open the website using the CloudFront domain configured in 5.7.1. Verify the homepage, banner, categories, and featured product list. Product data continues to load from Spring Boot through the CloudFront API path. Observed result: The GitHub Actions run completed with Success, and the CloudFront website displayed the Frontend, product images, and product data. The deployment preserved the image objects under the S3 images/ prefix.

title: Create Cognito User Pool
content:
Step 1 – Open Amazon Cognito In AWS Management Console, select Asia Pacific (Singapore) – ap-southeast-1. Open Amazon Cognito → User pools. The new AWS account initially has no user pools. Select Create user pool to open Set up resources for your application. Step 2 – Define the SPA application In Define your application, choose:
Field Value Application type Single-page application (SPA) Name your application techvina-frontend The TechVina React frontend runs in browsers and therefore uses a public client, without a client secret.
Step 3 – Configure sign-up and sign-in Under Configure options, select:
Field Value Options for sign-in identifiers Email only; do not select Phone number or Username Self-registration Enable self-registration Required attributes for sign-up email Add a return URL – optional Leave empty during initial creation Select Create user directory. This wizard creates the user pool, app client, and default managed-login domain together.
Step 4 – Rename the user pool Open the new user pool Overview. AWS may assign an initial name such as User pool - .... Select Rename and enter techvina-user-pool. Under User pool information, find the User pool ID, with the form ap-southeast-1_XXXXXXXXX. The pool in this deployment uses Region ap-southeast-1 and the Essentials plan. Step 5 – Verify the app client Open Applications → App clients → techvina-frontend. The wizard already created the client; do not create a duplicate.
Setting Observed configuration App client name techvina-frontend Client secret None (-) Authentication flows Choice-based sign-in, Secure Remote Password (SRP) Access token expiration 60 minutes ID token expiration 60 minutes Refresh token expiration 5 days Token revocation Enabled Record the Client ID for the backend and frontend configuration in later sections.
Step 6 – Verify the Cognito domain Open Branding → Domain in the user pool. The Cognito domain is already provisioned by AWS; Branding version is Managed login. No Custom domain is configured. Keep the AWS-provided domain. The Issuer type is Original. The managed-login domain follows this format:
https://<COGNITO_PREFIX>.auth.ap-southeast-1.amazoncognito.com The JWT issuer URL is derived from the user pool ID:
https://cognito-idp.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com/<USER_POOL_ID> Step 7 – Configure managed login and callback URL Open Applications → App clients → techvina-frontend → Login pages. Under Managed login pages configuration, select Edit. Configure: Field Value Allowed callback URLs http://localhost:5173/ Default redirect URL http://localhost:5173/ Identity providers Cognito user pool directory OAuth 2.0 grant types Authorization code grant OpenID Connect scopes openid, email, phone Allowed sign-out URLs Not configured at this stage If AWS has prefilled a CloudFront URL that does not belong to this deployment, replace it with http://localhost:5173/. Select Save changes and verify Status: Available.
These scopes match scope: "openid email phone" in frontend/src/services/authConfig.js. The SPA uses Authorization Code Flow with PKCE. Configure the deployed CloudFront HTTPS URL and sign-out URL later in 5.7.2.
Step 8 – Create Cognito groups Under User management → Groups, select Create group and create:
Group name Description Precedence IAM permissions ADMIN Quản trị viên hệ thống TechVina Blank Do not choose an IAM Role STAFF Nhân viên hệ thống TechVina Blank Do not choose an IAM Role CUSTOMER Khách hàng hệ thống TechVina Blank Do not choose an IAM Role Use the exact uppercase names. In backend/src/main/java/com/phoneshop/config/CognitoRoleConfig.java, the cognito:groups claim is mapped to ROLE_ADMIN, ROLE_STAFF, and ROLE_CUSTOMER.
Step 9 – Create an ADMIN account Open User management → Users → Create user. Select Invitation message: Send an email invitation. Enter an email address that you control; leave Phone number blank. Choose Temporary password → Generate a password. Select Create user. The new account initially shows Status: Enabled and Confirmation status: Force change password. For this deployment, the invitation Your temporary password arrived from no-reply@verificationemail.com.
Step 10 – Assign the ADMIN group Open the new account in Users. Under Group memberships, select Add user to group. Select only ADMIN, then Add. Verify Group memberships (1) with Group name: ADMIN. Step 11 – Sign in and change the temporary password Open Applications → App clients → techvina-frontend → View login page. On Sign in, enter the ADMIN email, select Next, and enter the temporary password from the invitation. On Change password, set and confirm a new password that meets the pool’s password policy. Return to Cognito → Users and select Refresh. The account changes to Confirmation status: Confirmed and remains Enabled. After the password change, Cognito redirects to http://localhost:5173/?code=.... The browser may report ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED because the frontend is not running on localhost. This does not indicate a failed password change. The code value is an authorization code, not an access token; no token exchange occurs while the frontend is unavailable.
Step 12 – Verify the ADMIN email During account creation, the email may initially remain Not verified even after the invitation was received.
Open Users → ADMIN account → User attributes → Edit. After confirming you control the mailbox, check Mark email address as verified. Save and verify Verified. The account remains in the ADMIN group. Step 13 – Verify email confirmation for self-registration Open Authentication → Sign-up and check:
Setting Value Cognito-assisted verification and confirmation Yes Attributes to verify Send email message, verify email address Required attributes email Custom attributes 0 Cognito is configured to send email verification messages to new self-registered users.
Step 14 – Check password policy and MFA Under Authentication → Authentication methods → Password policy:
Setting Value Password minimum length 8 characters Password requirements Uppercase, lowercase, number, special character Temporary password expiry 7 days Under Authentication → Sign-in → Multi-factor authentication, the observed configuration is No MFA. Keep this setting for this deployment and select Cancel after inspection.
Step 15 – Cognito values for the backend Use the values from the current AWS account to complete backend/.env in 5.5.3:
COGNITO_ISSUER_URI=https://cognito-idp.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com/<USER_POOL_ID> COGNITO_CLIENT_ID=<APP_CLIENT_ID> COGNITO_DOMAIN=https://<COGNITO_PREFIX>.auth.ap-southeast-1.amazoncognito.com Result: techvina-user-pool, a public techvina-frontend app client without a client secret, managed login, ADMIN/STAFF/CUSTOMER groups, and an ADMIN account marked Confirmed, Enabled, and email Verified.

title: Deploy Backend Spring Boot with CI/CD
content:
Step 1 – Verify the Backend on EC2 before deployment The TechVina Backend runs as a Spring Boot application on the techvina-ec2-backend EC2 instance (Ubuntu 24.04) in Singapore (ap-southeast-1). The existing techvina-backend.service was configured in section 5.5. GitHub Actions updates the deployed JAR without recreating the EC2 instance or the RDS database.
Open AWS Systems Manager → Session Manager and connect to the Backend instance. Verify the service and HTTP health endpoint: sudo systemctl is-active techvina-backend.service active curl -sS --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health {"status":"UP"} Verify that AWS CLI, the JAR validation utility and the deployment lock utility are available: aws --version The AWS CLI version recorded during deployment was v2.35.21. The utility checks returned:
command -v flock /usr/bin/flock command -v unzip /usr/bin/unzip If unzip is not installed, install it on Ubuntu and verify the path:
sudo apt-get install -y unzip command -v unzip /usr/bin/unzip The EC2 instance role techvina-ec2-ssm-role grants s3:GetObject on releases/* in the Backend Artifacts bucket. The GitHub Actions Backend role and OIDC trust configuration were created in section 5.8.1.
Step 2 – Prepare the GitHub workflow and deployment scripts Open the TechVina repository in VS Code and work on the master branch. The deployment-related files are:
TechVina/ ├── backend/ │ ├── pom.xml │ └── src/ └── .github/ ├── workflows/ │ └── deploy-backend.yml ├── scripts/ │ └── deploy-backend.sh └── tests/ └── test-backend-rollback.sh The techvina-backend-artifacts-<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID> bucket stores two artifacts under releases/:
releases/backend-<COMMIT_SHA>.jar releases/deploy-backend-<COMMIT_SHA>.sh In the configuration examples below, replace <AWS_ACCOUNT_ID> with the AWS account ID and <EC2_INSTANCE_ID> with the actual Backend EC2 instance ID. The deployed resources were verified in ap-southeast-1.
Step 3 – Configure the deployment, backup and rollback script Open .github/scripts/deploy-backend.sh. The script downloads the JAR identified by a commit SHA, validates its archive structure with unzip, backs up the live JAR and restarts the Spring Boot service through systemctl. If deployment fails after the JAR replacement begins, the on_exit() handler restores the backup and checks /actuator/health. A flock lock prevents overlapping deployments.
Use the following script and replace <AWS_ACCOUNT_ID> with the account used for deployment:
#!/usr/bin/env bash set -Eeuo pipefail # Cau hinh TechVina Backend BASE="/home/ubuntu/projects/TechVina/backend" LIVE="$BASE/target/backend-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar" SERVICE="techvina-backend.service" BACKUP_DIR="$BASE/backups" BUCKET="techvina-backend-artifacts-<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>" REGION="ap-southeast-1" HEALTH_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health" # Nhan commit SHA tu GitHub Actions COMMIT_SHA="${1:-}" if [[ ! "$COMMIT_SHA" =~ ^[a-f0-9]{40}$ ]]; then echo "ERROR: Invalid commit SHA" exit 1 fi # Script phai chay voi quyen root if [[ "$EUID" -ne 0 ]]; then echo "ERROR: Root permission required" exit 1 fi # Ngan hai lan trien khai chay dong thoi exec 9>/run/lock/techvina-backend-deploy.lock flock -n 9 || { echo "ERROR: Another deployment is running" exit 1 } # Tao thu muc sao luu install -d -o ubuntu -g ubuntu -m 700 "$BACKUP_DIR" NEW_JAR=$(mktemp "$BASE/target/.deploy-XXXXXX.jar") BACKUP="" SWITCH_STARTED=false DEPLOY_OK=false # Kiem tra trang thai ung dung wait_for_health() { for i in $(seq 1 45); do RESPONSE=$(curl -fsS --max-time 3 \ "$HEALTH_URL" 2>/dev/null || true) if [[ "$RESPONSE" == '{"status":"UP"}' ]]; then return 0 fi sleep 2 done return 1 } # Tu dong rollback neu trien khai that bai on_exit() { STATUS=$? trap - EXIT rm -f "$NEW_JAR" if [[ "$SWITCH_STARTED" == true && "$DEPLOY_OK" == false ]]; then echo "DEPLOY FAILED - Starting rollback" systemctl stop "$SERVICE" || true if install -o ubuntu -g ubuntu -m 600 \ "$BACKUP" "$LIVE" && systemctl start "$SERVICE"; then if wait_for_health; then echo "ROLLBACK SUCCESS" else echo "ERROR: Rollback health check failed" fi else echo "ERROR: Could not restore Backend" fi STATUS=1 fi exit "$STATUS" } trap on_exit EXIT echo "Deploying commit: $COMMIT_SHA" # Buoc 1: Tai JAR moi tu Amazon S3 aws s3 cp \ "s3://$BUCKET/releases/backend-$COMMIT_SHA.jar" \ "$NEW_JAR" \ --region "$REGION" \ --only-show-errors # Buoc 2: Kiem tra file JAR test -s "$NEW_JAR" unzip -tq "$NEW_JAR" >/dev/null # Buoc 3: Kiem tra Backend hien tai test -s "$LIVE" systemctl is-active --quiet "$SERVICE" # Buoc 4: Sao luu phien ban dang chay BACKUP=$(mktemp \ "$BACKUP_DIR/backend-before-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-XXXXXX.jar") install -o ubuntu -g ubuntu -m 600 "$LIVE" "$BACKUP" echo "Backup saved: $BACKUP" # Buoc 5: Thay the JAR va khoi dong lai SWITCH_STARTED=true systemctl stop "$SERVICE" install -o ubuntu -g ubuntu -m 600 \ "$NEW_JAR" "$LIVE" systemctl start "$SERVICE" # Buoc 6: Kiem tra Health Check echo "Checking Backend health..." if wait_for_health; then DEPLOY_OK=true echo "DEPLOY SUCCESS" echo "Commit: $COMMIT_SHA" echo "Health: $RESPONSE" else echo "ERROR: Backend health check failed" exit 1 fi # Buoc 7: Don dep Backup cu sau khi Deploy thanh cong echo "Cleaning up old Backend backups..." # Lay danh sach Backup tu dong, moi nhat truoc mapfile -t BACKUPS < <( find "$BACKUP_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f \ -name 'backend-before-????????T??????Z-*.jar' \ -printf '%f\n' | LC_ALL=C sort -r ) # Chi giu lai 3 ban Backup tu dong moi nhat if (( ${#BACKUPS[@]} > 3 )); then for OLD_BACKUP in "${BACKUPS[@]:3}"; do rm -f -- "$BACKUP_DIR/$OLD_BACKUP" || echo "WARNING: Could not delete $OLD_BACKUP" done fi echo "Backup cleanup completed" After a successful deployment, the script retains up to the three newest automatically created backups in backend/backups/. Rollback on the actual EC2 instance is only attempted if an error occurs after the JAR switch has started; no rollback happened during the successful deployment.
Step 4 – Test rollback behavior using a mock environment Open .github/tests/test-backend-rollback.sh. The test extracts the actual deployment script’s on_exit() function, but mocks systemctl, install, JAR files and the health check in a temporary directory. It never stops the production Backend on EC2.
#!/usr/bin/env bash set -Eeuo pipefail # Xac dinh thu muc project ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)" DEPLOY_SCRIPT="$ROOT/.github/scripts/deploy-backend.sh" # Tao moi truong thu nghiem tam TEST_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" trap 'rm -rf "$TEST_DIR"' EXIT LIVE="$TEST_DIR/backend.jar" BACKUP="$TEST_DIR/backend-backup.jar" NEW_JAR="$TEST_DIR/backend-new.jar" SERVICE="techvina-backend.service" # Gia lap JAR cu va JAR moi bi loi printf 'BACKEND_VERSION_OK\n' > "$BACKUP" printf 'BACKEND_VERSION_FAILED\n' > "$LIVE" printf 'TEMPORARY_JAR\n' > "$NEW_JAR" SWITCH_STARTED=true DEPLOY_OK=false # Gia lap systemctl, khong dung den EC2 systemctl() { case "$1" in stop|start) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac } # Gia lap lenh install de khoi phuc file install() { local source_file="${@: -2:1}" local target_file="${@: -1}" cp "$source_file" "$target_file" } # Gia lap Health Check sau Rollback wait_for_health() { cmp -s "$LIVE" "$BACKUP" } # Lay ham Rollback tu script trien khai that source <(sed -n '/^on_exit() {/,/^}/p' "$DEPLOY_SCRIPT") # Gia lap trien khai that bai set +e OUTPUT="$( (set +e; false; on_exit) 2>&1 )" EXIT_CODE=$? set -e # Xac minh ket qua Rollback [[ "$EXIT_CODE" -eq 1 ]] [[ "$OUTPUT" == *"ROLLBACK SUCCESS"* ]] cmp -s "$LIVE" "$BACKUP" [[ ! -e "$NEW_JAR" ]] echo "ROLLBACK_TEST_OK" echo "Exit code: $EXIT_CODE" echo "Backup restored successfully" echo "Temporary JAR removed" From the repository root, open Git Bash in VS Code on Windows and run:
bash .github/tests/test-backend-rollback.sh Actual Git Bash output:
ROLLBACK_TEST_OK Exit code: 1 Backup restored successfully Temporary JAR removed Exit code: 1 is the intentionally simulated failed deployment. The overall rollback test reports ROLLBACK_TEST_OK. This confirms the rollback logic in the mock environment, not a deliberately induced production EC2 failure.
Step 5 – Configure the Backend GitHub Actions workflow Open .github/workflows/deploy-backend.yml. This workflow uses Java 21, Maven, OIDC and SSM to deploy to the EC2 instance. The full workflow configuration is:
name: Build TechVina Backend on: push: branches: - master paths: - "backend/**" - ".github/workflows/deploy-backend.yml" - ".github/scripts/**" - ".github/tests/**" workflow_dispatch: inputs: deploy: description: "Deploy Backend to EC2" type: boolean required: true default: false permissions: contents: read id-token: write concurrency: group: deploy-techvina-backend cancel-in-progress: false jobs: build: name: Build Spring Boot Backend runs-on: ubuntu-latest defaults: run: working-directory: backend steps: # Bước 1: Lấy source code - name: Checkout source code uses: actions/checkout@v7 # Bước 2: Cài đặt Java 21 - name: Setup Java 21 uses: actions/setup-java@v6 with: distribution: temurin java-version: "21" cache: maven cache-dependency-path: backend/pom.xml # Bước 3: Build Spring Boot bằng Maven - name: Build Backend run: mvn -B -ntp clean package -DskipTests # Bước 4: Kiểm tra file JAR - name: Verify JAR file run: test -s target/backend-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar # Kiểm tra thông tin OIDC thực tế - name: Debug OIDC claims uses: actions/github-script@v8 with: script: | const token = await core.getIDToken('sts.amazonaws.com'); const payload = JSON.parse( Buffer.from(token.split('.')[1], 'base64url').toString('utf8') ); core.info('OIDC sub: ' + payload.sub); core.info('OIDC aud: ' + payload.aud); core.info('OIDC iss: ' + payload.iss); # Bước 5: Xác thực AWS bằng GitHub OIDC - name: Configure AWS credentials uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6.3.0 with: role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:role/techvina-github-actions-backend-role aws-region: ap-southeast-1 # Bước 6: Kiểm tra xác thực AWS - name: Verify AWS identity run: aws sts get-caller-identity # Bước 7: Upload file JAR lên Amazon S3 - name: Upload Backend JAR to S3 run: | aws s3 cp target/backend-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar \ "s3://techvina-backend-artifacts-<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>/releases/backend-${GITHUB_SHA}.jar" \ --region ap-southeast-1 \ --no-progress \ --only-show-errors # Kiem tra cu phap script trien khai - name: Validate Backend deployment script run: bash -n "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/deploy-backend.sh" # Kiem thu logic Rollback - name: Test backend rollback logic shell: bash run: | set -euo pipefail bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/tests/test-backend-rollback.sh" # Upload script trien khai len Amazon S3 - name: Upload Backend deployment script to S3 run: | aws s3 cp \ "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/deploy-backend.sh" \ "s3://techvina-backend-artifacts-<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>/releases/deploy-backend-${GITHUB_SHA}.sh" \ --region ap-southeast-1 \ --no-progress \ --only-show-errors # Bước 8: Kiểm tra GitHub Actions gửi lệnh đến EC2 - name: Verify SSM connection to EC2 run: | COMMAND_ID=$(aws ssm send-command \ --instance-ids <EC2_INSTANCE_ID> \ --document-name AWS-RunShellScript \ --parameters 'commands=["echo TechVina SSM connection OK"]' \ --region ap-southeast-1 \ --query 'Command.CommandId' \ --output text) echo "SSM Command ID: $COMMAND_ID" aws ssm wait command-executed \ --command-id "$COMMAND_ID" \ --instance-id <EC2_INSTANCE_ID> \ --region ap-southeast-1 aws ssm get-command-invocation \ --command-id "$COMMAND_ID" \ --instance-id <EC2_INSTANCE_ID> \ --region ap-southeast-1 \ --query '{Status:Status,Output:StandardOutputContent}' \ --output json # Bước 9: Kiểm tra script triển khai trên EC2 qua SSM - name: Verify deployment script on EC2 shell: bash run: | set -euo pipefail cat > ssm-script-check.json <<EOF { "commands": [ "aws s3 cp s3://techvina-backend-artifacts-<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>/releases/deploy-backend-${GITHUB_SHA}.sh /tmp/deploy-backend-${GITHUB_SHA}.sh --region ap-southeast-1 --only-show-errors && bash -n /tmp/deploy-backend-${GITHUB_SHA}.sh && echo SSM_SCRIPT_CHECK_OK" ] } EOF COMMAND_ID=$(aws ssm send-command \ --instance-ids <EC2_INSTANCE_ID> \ --document-name AWS-RunShellScript \ --parameters file://ssm-script-check.json \ --region ap-southeast-1 \ --query 'Command.CommandId' \ --output text) echo "SSM Command ID: $COMMAND_ID" aws ssm wait command-executed \ --command-id "$COMMAND_ID" \ --instance-id <EC2_INSTANCE_ID> \ --region ap-southeast-1 aws ssm get-command-invocation \ --command-id "$COMMAND_ID" \ --instance-id <EC2_INSTANCE_ID> \ --region ap-southeast-1 \ --query '{Status:Status,Output:StandardOutputContent}' \ --output json # Buoc 10: Tu dong trien khai Backend qua SSM - name: Deploy Backend to EC2 via SSM if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' && (github.event_name == 'push' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.deploy == true)) }} shell: bash run: | set -euo pipefail INSTANCE_ID="<EC2_INSTANCE_ID>" REGION="ap-southeast-1" # Tao lenh SSM de tai va chay script cat > ssm-deploy.json <<EOF { "commands": [ "aws s3 cp s3://techvina-backend-artifacts-<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>/releases/deploy-backend-${GITHUB_SHA}.sh /tmp/deploy-backend-${GITHUB_SHA}.sh --region ${REGION} --only-show-errors && bash -n /tmp/deploy-backend-${GITHUB_SHA}.sh && sudo bash /tmp/deploy-backend-${GITHUB_SHA}.sh ${GITHUB_SHA}" ], "executionTimeout": ["600"] } EOF COMMAND_ID=$(aws ssm send-command \ --instance-ids "$INSTANCE_ID" \ --document-name AWS-RunShellScript \ --parameters file://ssm-deploy.json \ --region "$REGION" \ --query 'Command.CommandId' \ --output text) echo "SSM Command ID: $COMMAND_ID" # Theo doi qua trinh trien khai STATUS="Pending" for i in $(seq 1 60); do STATUS=$(aws ssm get-command-invocation \ --command-id "$COMMAND_ID" \ --instance-id "$INSTANCE_ID" \ --region "$REGION" \ --query Status \ --output text 2>/dev/null || echo Pending) case "$STATUS" in Success|Failed|Cancelled|TimedOut|DeliveryTimedOut|ExecutionTimedOut|Undeliverable|Terminated) break ;; esac sleep 10 done # Hien thi ket qua trien khai aws ssm get-command-invocation \ --command-id "$COMMAND_ID" \ --instance-id "$INSTANCE_ID" \ --region "$REGION" \ --query '{Status:Status,ResponseCode:ResponseCode,Output:StandardOutputContent,Error:StandardErrorContent}' \ --output json test "$STATUS" = "Success" Execution sequence: Checkout source code → Setup Java 21 → mvn clean package -DskipTests → JAR verification → AWS OIDC authentication → JAR upload to S3 → deployment script validation and mocked rollback test → script upload to S3 → SSM connectivity and remote script checks → deployment through SSM.
The push trigger handles changes under backend/**, .github/workflows/deploy-backend.yml, .github/scripts/** and .github/tests/** on master. The workflow_dispatch input deploy defaults to false, but this skips only the final deployment step: build, artifact uploads and SSM verification steps still run.
Step 6 – Review changes, commit and push In Git Bash at the TechVina repository root, review the updated deployment files:
git --no-pager diff -- .github/workflows/deploy-backend.yml .github/scripts/deploy-backend.sh Ensure that the Backend role ARN, S3 bucket name and EC2 instance ID refer to the resources provisioned in your AWS account. Stage the updates:
git add .github/workflows/deploy-backend.yml .github/scripts/deploy-backend.sh git status --short Actual Git Bash output:
M .github/scripts/deploy-backend.sh M .github/workflows/deploy-backend.yml Commit the changes:
git commit -m "ci: update backend deployment workflow for AWS" [master 64b4a47] ci: update backend deployment workflow for AWS 2 files changed, 13 insertions(+), 13 deletions(-) Push the commit to the deployment branch:
git push origin master This push triggers the Backend deployment workflow. When its deploy step runs, it replaces the live EC2 JAR and restarts Spring Boot. Verify that the current Backend is healthy before pushing.
Step 7 – Verify GitHub Actions and the SSM deployment results Open GitHub → Actions → Build TechVina Backend and select the run for commit 64b4a47. Verify that Build Spring Boot Backend completed the Maven build, OIDC authentication, S3 artifact uploads, rollback test and Deploy Backend to EC2 via SSM. Expand Deploy Backend to EC2 via SSM to inspect the SSM command status, JAR backup and health check. Actual deployment result: Success – 1 minute 28 seconds.
Actual SSM and deployment script output (excerpt):
SSM command status: Success ResponseCode: 0 Deploying commit: 64b4a4732f64cac5dd7934982d0bfc3e0cbb74d5 Backup saved: /home/ubuntu/projects/TechVina/backend/backups/backend-before-20261113T152128Z-Suq5VZ.jar Checking Backend health... DEPLOY SUCCESS Commit: 64b4a4732f64cac5dd7934982d0bfc3e0cbb74d5 Health: {"status":"UP"} Cleaning up old Backend backups... Backup cleanup completed The backup file was created before the live JAR was replaced. Spring Boot subsequently restarted and returned {"status":"UP"}. The DEPLOY SUCCESS output confirms that this release succeeded without entering rollback.
Step 8 – Verify the Backend and website after deployment On EC2, use Session Manager to verify the Backend service and health endpoint:
sudo systemctl is-active techvina-backend.service curl -sS --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health active {"status":"UP"} Open the website through CloudFront, browse the product list and open a product detail page. During the TechVina verification, the Xiaomi 15 page loaded product details, variants, colors, images and inventory information from the application.
The GitHub Actions pipeline built the JAR with Maven, uploaded the artifacts to S3, sent the SSM command to EC2, created a backup, replaced the JAR, restarted Spring Boot and passed its health check. The website and product data remained accessible after deployment.

title: Integrate and deploy Frontend, Backend, Cognito
content:
Step 1 – Prepare Node.js and frontend source on EC2 Connect to techvina-ec2-backend using Session Manager, switch to ubuntu, and inspect the frontend:
sudo -iu ubuntu cd /home/ubuntu/projects/TechVina/frontend cat package.json TechVina uses React 19, Vite 8, react-oidc-context, and oidc-client-ts. The EC2 instance initially did not have Node.js; NodeSource 24.x was installed:
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_24.x | sudo -E bash - sudo apt install -y nodejs node --version npm --version Actual versions: Node.js v24.22.3, npm 11.19.1.
Step 2 – Configure frontend environment variables From /home/ubuntu/projects/TechVina/frontend, inspect the example file:
cat .env.example Create .env in the same directory:
nano .env Use values for your AWS account:
VITE_AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-1 VITE_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID=<COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID> VITE_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID=<COGNITO_CLIENT_ID> VITE_COGNITO_DOMAIN=https://<COGNITO_PREFIX>.auth.ap-southeast-1.amazoncognito.com VITE_COGNITO_REDIRECT_URI=https://<CF_DOMAIN>/ VITE_COGNITO_LOGOUT_URI=https://<CF_DOMAIN>/ VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://<CF_DOMAIN> Actual TechVina API base URL:
VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://d3mmtr3bxttvgc.cloudfront.net Do not add a trailing / to VITE_API_BASE_URL. frontend/src/services/api.js concatenates the Base URL with endpoints that already begin with /:
fetch(`${BASE_URL}${endpoint}`, { A trailing slash in the Base URL creates //api/..., which does not match the intended /api/* behavior. In contrast, the Redirect and Logout URLs must have their trailing / to match the Cognito callback and sign-out settings from 5.7.2.
Verify:
grep '^VITE_API_BASE_URL=' .env Keep .env out of Git. Never put DB passwords, JWT secrets, or AWS Access Keys in VITE_* variables: Vite exposes them in the compiled browser JavaScript.
Step 3 – Install dependencies and build React/Vite From frontend:
npm ci npm audit The actual initial audit found two high severity advisories affecting vite and source-map-js. They were resolved with:
npm audit fix npm audit Actual result: found 0 vulnerabilities. npm audit fix changes dependency versions and package-lock.json. Commit the updated lockfile to GitHub before configuring CI/CD in 5.8.2 so GitHub Actions’ npm ci installs the same resolved versions.
Build for production:
npm run build Actual result: Vite v8.3.8, 390 modules transformed, ✓ built in 1.40s. The rebuilt bundle after correcting the API URL included dist/assets/index-BJaK_frI.js.
Inspect:
ls -lah dist ls -lah dist/images The build must contain dist/index.html, dist/assets/, dist/images/, and dist/favicon.svg.
Step 4 – Verify EC2 IAM permissions for frontend S3 uploads Install AWS CLI v2 on the Ubuntu x86_64 instance before running aws s3:
cd /tmp curl -fsSLO https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip unzip -oq awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip sudo ./aws/install --update aws --version If AWS CLI v2 is already installed, check aws --version and do not repeat the installation.

[Unit] Description=TechVina Spring Boot Backend After=network-online.target Wants=network-online.target [Service] Type=simple User=ubuntu Group=ubuntu WorkingDirectory=/home/ubuntu/projects/TechVina/backend EnvironmentFile=/home/ubuntu/projects/TechVina/backend/.env ExecStart=/usr/bin/java -jar /home/ubuntu/projects/TechVina/backend/target/backend-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar --spring.jpa.show-sql=false --logging.level.org.hibernate.orm.jdbc.bind=OFF --logging.level.org.hibernate.SQL=WARN --logging.level.org.springframework.security=INFO --logging.level.org.springframework.web=INFO --logging.level.org.springframework.web.servlet.mvc.method.annotation.RequestMappingHandlerMapping=INFO Restart=on-failure RestartSec=5 SuccessExitStatus=143 [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target Save using Ctrl + O → Enter → Ctrl + X. title: CloudWatch Monitoring and System Validation
content:
Step 1 – Inspect Spring Boot logs on the EC2 instance The TechVina Backend runs on the techvina-ec2-backend EC2 instance in Singapore (ap-southeast-1). Spring Boot is managed by the techvina-backend.service systemd unit. The EC2 IAM role, techvina-ec2-ssm-role, includes CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy, allowing the instance to send monitoring data to Amazon CloudWatch.
Open AWS Systems Manager → Session Manager and connect to the Backend instance. Inspect the service’s logging destination: sudo systemctl show techvina-backend.service -p StandardOutput -p StandardError EC2 output:
StandardOutput=journal StandardError=inherit Spring Boot therefore writes to the systemd journal. Inspect its recent log entries:
sudo journalctl -u techvina-backend.service -n 15 --no-pager Selected lines from the observed output:
Nov 13 15:21:46 ip-10-20-1-19 java[26448]: 2026-11-13T15:21:46.308Z INFO 26448 --- [ main] o.s.b.w.embedded.tomcat.TomcatWebServer : Tomcat started on port 8080 (http) with context path '/' Nov 13 15:21:46 ip-10-20-1-19 java[26448]: 2026-11-13T15:21:46.333Z INFO 26448 --- [ main] com.phoneshop.BackendApplication : Started BackendApplication in 15.814 seconds (process running for 16.912) The CloudWatch Agent can collect these entries directly from journald. There is no need to create /var/log/techvina/backend.log or change Spring Boot’s systemd logging configuration.
Step 2 – Install the Amazon CloudWatch Agent Check whether the Agent is installed:
systemctl status amazon-cloudwatch-agent --no-pager Output before installation:
Unit amazon-cloudwatch-agent.service could not be found. Download the official Ubuntu amd64 package:
wget -O /tmp/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.deb https://amazoncloudwatch-agent.s3.amazonaws.com/ubuntu/amd64/latest/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.deb Observed download output:
HTTP request sent, awaiting response... 200 OK Length: 77725146 (74M) [application/octet-stream] Saving to: ‘/tmp/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.deb’ ‘/tmp/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.deb’ saved [77725146/77725146] Install the downloaded package:
sudo dpkg -i /tmp/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.deb EC2 output:
Selecting previously unselected package amazon-cloudwatch-agent. Unpacking amazon-cloudwatch-agent (1.300074.1b2005-1) ... Setting up amazon-cloudwatch-agent (1.300074.1b2005-1) ... Step 3 – Configure the Agent to collect journald logs From Session Manager, create /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json:
sudo tee /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json > /dev/null <<'EOF' { "agent": { "region": "ap-southeast-1" }, "logs": { "logs_collected": { "journald": { "collect_list": [ { "log_group_name": "/techvina/backend/application", "log_stream_name": "{instance_id}", "units": ["techvina-backend.service"], "retention_in_days": 7 } ] } } } } EOF units restricts collection to techvina-backend.service. log_group_name sends events to /techvina/backend/application. log_stream_name uses the EC2 Instance ID as the log stream name. retention_in_days stores logs for 7 days. Load the configuration and start the Agent:
sudo /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -a fetch-config -m ec2 -s -c file:/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json Configuration validation output:
I! Valid Json input schema. Configuration validation first phase succeeded Configuration validation second phase succeeded Configuration validation succeeded Confirm the Agent is running:
sudo systemctl status amazon-cloudwatch-agent --no-pager Relevant observed output:
Loaded: loaded (/etc/systemd/system/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.service; enabled; preset: enabled) Active: active (running) since Sat 2026-11-14 05:39:44 UTC Main PID: 31283 (amazon-cloudwat) CGroup: /system.slice/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.service ├─31283 /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent ... └─31330 journalctl --utc --output=json --follow --lines=0 --unit techvina-backend.service --priority info The collector uses --lines=0 and --follow, so it initially processes new log events. In the actual setup, the following check found no new service entries:
sudo journalctl -u techvina-backend.service --since "2026-11-14 05:39:44 UTC" --no-pager -- No entries -- To generate fresh startup events for verification, the Backend service was restarted through Session Manager:
sudo systemctl restart techvina-backend.service Restarting briefly interrupts the Backend during application startup, but does not replace the JAR or modify the database. The restarted application generated new events, which the Agent collected.
Step 4 – Verify application logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs Open CloudWatch → Logs → Log management → Log groups in ap-southeast-1. Open /techvina/backend/application. Verify Log Class Standard and a retention of 1 week. Select the log stream named after the techvina-ec2-backend Instance ID. Open Log events and inspect entries from Hibernate, JPA, Tomcat and Spring Boot startup. The received events include Initialized JPA EntityManagerFactory, Tomcat started on port 8080 and Started BackendApplication. This confirms the EC2 → journald → CloudWatch Agent → CloudWatch Logs collection path.
Step 5 – Monitor EC2 metrics using CloudWatch Open CloudWatch → Metrics → Classic metrics. Select EC2 → Per-Instance Metrics. Locate the instance by its InstanceId and techvina-ec2-backend name. Select CPUUtilization and display the graph over 3h. The chart shows the instance’s actual CPU usage, including a brief rise near the end of the selected period. The Per-Instance Metrics page also provides StatusCheckFailed, NetworkIn, NetworkOut and CPUCreditBalance for the T3 EC2 instance.
Step 6 – Create a CloudWatch Alarm and configure Amazon SNS With the CPUUtilization metric selected, choose Create alarm and configure:
Setting Value Namespace / Metric AWS/EC2 / CPUUtilization EC2 instance techvina-ec2-backend Statistic Average Period 5 minutes Threshold type Static Condition Greater than 70 (%) Datapoints to alarm 2 out of 2 Missing data treatment Treat missing data as missing Evaluation window Default (Sliding window) Alarm name techvina-backend-high-cpu Both consecutive 5-minute averages must exceed 70% for the alarm to transition to ALARM.
Under Configure actions → Notification:
Select In alarm. Choose Create new topic and enter techvina-backend-cpu-alerts. Enter the notification email address and select Create topic. Open the AWS Notifications confirmation email and choose Confirm subscription. Under Add alarm details, set the alarm name to techvina-backend-high-cpu and enter: Monitor CPU utilization of the TechVina Backend EC2 instance. Trigger an alarm when average CPU utilization exceeds 70% for 2 consecutive 5-minute periods. Send an email notification through Amazon SNS. Review Preview and create, then select Create alarm. Open Amazon SNS → Topics → techvina-backend-cpu-alerts and verify that the email subscription has Confirmed status and uses the EMAIL protocol.
Step 7 – Verify the Alarm state and test SNS email delivery After creation, techvina-backend-high-cpu initially displayed Insufficient data, then changed to OK once enough CPU datapoints were evaluated. On the Actions tab, the configuration shows Actions enabled and a notification sent to techvina-backend-cpu-alerts when the alarm enters the ALARM state.
To test email delivery without increasing EC2 CPU load:
Open Amazon SNS → Topics → techvina-backend-cpu-alerts → Publish message. Enter the Subject: TechVina - SNS Notification Test Choose Identical payload for all delivery protocols, then enter the Message body: TECHVINA SNS NOTIFICATION TEST This is a test notification from Amazon SNS. SNS Topic: techvina-backend-cpu-alerts CloudWatch Alarm: techvina-backend-high-cpu EC2 Instance: techvina-ec2-backend Result: Testing email notification delivery. Select Publish message and open the subscribed mailbox. The test message was successfully delivered by AWS Notifications. This test verifies SNS email delivery to a confirmed subscription. It does not test a real CPU threshold breach or an actual transition into ALARM.
Step 8 – Validate the Backend and website after deployment Use Session Manager to check Spring Boot health:
curl -sS --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health Observed EC2 output:
{"status":"UP"} Open the TechVina site through CloudFront and verify the home page, categories, featured product list and Xiaomi 15 product details. These user-facing checks were carried out after the Backend CI/CD deployment in 5.8.3 and are documented in 5.8.2 and 5.8.3.
Component Verified result Frontend GitHub Actions Successful workflow in 5.8.2 Backend GitHub Actions DEPLOY SUCCESS, SSM ResponseCode: 0, Health UP in 5.8.3 CloudWatch Agent active (running); collecting journald CloudWatch Logs Spring Boot log group, stream and events available CloudWatch Metrics EC2 CPUUtilization chart populated CloudWatch Alarm 70% threshold configured, OK state, SNS action enabled Amazon SNS Email subscription Confirmed; test email received Website Homepage, featured products and product details displayed following deployment

title: Clean Up AWS Resources
content:
Step 1 – Prepare and identify resources for deletion TechVina was deployed in Asia Pacific (Singapore) – ap-southeast-1, using Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS for MySQL, Amazon S3, Amazon CloudFront, Amazon Cognito, Amazon VPC, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon SNS, and IAM. After deployment and testing are complete, remove the resources created for the workshop.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console and select Singapore (ap-southeast-1). Verify each resource’s name and ID before deletion. Open GitHub → TaiHoang69/TechVina → Actions. Disable the Frontend and Backend deployment workflows to prevent later pushes from triggering new AWS deployments. Download the data that must be preserved, including source code, MySQL SQL exports, product images, workshop documents, and required deployment files. Verify the local copies before deleting data in AWS. Identify the main resources: Service TechVina resources Amazon EC2 techvina-ec2-backend Amazon RDS MySQL database and techvina-db-subnet-group Amazon S3 techvina-frontend-668668940018, techvina-backend-artifacts-668668940018 Amazon CloudFront Distribution E12UZ3V9Z7AGAU and Origin Access Control (OAC) Amazon Cognito techvina-user-pool Amazon CloudWatch Alarm techvina-backend-high-cpu, Log Group /techvina/backend/application Amazon SNS Topic techvina-backend-cpu-alerts Amazon VPC techvina-vpc and its networking components AWS IAM EC2 and GitHub Actions IAM roles and GitHub OIDC provider Step 2 – Delete Amazon CloudFront resources Open Amazon CloudFront → Distributions and select the TechVina distribution (E12UZ3V9Z7AGAU). Choose Disable and confirm. When the update has finished deploying, choose Delete to remove the distribution. Open CloudFront → Functions. If techvina-spa-routing exists, verify that it is no longer associated with any distribution, then delete it. Open CloudFront → Origin access. Locate the OAC used for the Frontend S3 origin. Once no other distribution uses it, delete the OAC. Return to Distributions and confirm the TechVina distribution is no longer listed. Step 3 – Terminate the Backend EC2 instance and remove related resources Open Amazon EC2 → Instances, select techvina-ec2-backend (i-0de916c9bd054d655). Inspect its EBS volume on the Storage tab. Choose Instance state → Terminate (delete) instance and confirm. When the instance becomes Terminated, open EC2 → Volumes. If a TechVina volume remains and is no longer in use, select Actions → Delete volume. Open EC2 → Snapshots and AMIs and use the Owned by me filter. Delete TechVina-specific snapshots or AMIs if any remain; deregister an AMI before deleting dependent snapshots where necessary. Open EC2 → Elastic IPs. Disassociate and release any Elastic IP specifically allocated for TechVina. Inspect EC2 → Network Interfaces to confirm that no interface belonging to the Backend instance remains. Interfaces owned by another AWS service should be removed through that service. Step 4 – Delete the RDS MySQL database and related resources Open Amazon RDS → Databases in Singapore and select the TechVina MySQL database. If Deletion protection is enabled, use Modify to turn it off. Choose Actions → Delete. Once any necessary data has been exported outside AWS, choose not to create a Final snapshot and not to retain Automated backups, then confirm.
